claim: TokenRepair uses context-aware token-level uncertainty fluctuations to localize likely-faulty tokens in a patch and rewrites only those, then filters low-quality patches by external feedback; it fixes 88 bugs on Defects4J 1.2 and 139 on HumanEval-Java.
stance_target: L4 localization + targeted repair is partially occupied at token granularity (uncertainty-guided)
scope_conditions: Single-hunk APR, ground-truth hunk location given
quoted_support: TokenRepair achieves new state-of-the-art repair performance, correctly fixing 88 bugs on Defects4J 1.2 and 139 bugs on HumanEval-Java, demonstrating substantial improvements ranging from 8.2% to 34.9% across all models on Defects4J 1.2 and from 3.3% to 16.1% on HumanEval-Java.

breadth.confidence_families: Token-level uncertainty from output probabilities: suspiciousness score with decay factor alpha, plus patch-level quality metrics (RQ1, Table 1)
breadth.base_vs_instruct: not present (searched: all five are instruct)
breadth.elicitation_formats: Token log-prob uncertainty; Chain-of-Thought-guided rewriting; no verbalized confidence (searched: verbal 0)
breadth.benchmarks: Defects4J 1.2 (154 single-hunk bugs) and HumanEval-Java (163 pairs) (Sec 4.1.2)
breadth.label_source: Test execution plus manual verification of plausible patches by three researchers (Threats to Validity)
breadth.label_independence: Fault location (buggy hunk) provided from ground truth (Sec 4.1.2)
breadth.calibration_metrics: Top-K localization accuracy (Top-1 about 0.41-0.48, avg 0.589-0.695, Table 1); correct-fix counts; no ECE
breadth.granularity: Token level within a patch; patch-level quality filter
breadth.causal_intervention: Ablation of components (RQ3): removing uncertainty-guided localization drops performance by 20.6%

claim: Token suspiciousness scores localize faulty tokens with average Top-K accuracy 0.589 to 0.695 across models and decay settings, evidence of a correlation between uncertainty scores and patch correctness.
quoted_support: achieving average localization accuracy ranging from 0.589 to 0.695, indicating promising effectiveness of uncertainty-guided token-level fault localization

claim: The work motivates its signal by citing Spiess et al. 2024 that high-uncertainty code tokens are more often wrong, and relies on coarse test pass/fail as the external feedback it improves on.
stance_target: prior art chain for token-level confidence
quoted_support: Their findings reveal strong calibration between entropy-based uncertainty metrics and the correctness of generated code tokens across multiple LLMs.

claim: Evaluation uses temperature 1, patch budget capped at 50, and the repair terminates when a plausible patch is found; no per-requirement or test-group confidence is used and no verbalized confidence is elicited.
stance_target: L4 per-requirement/test-group confidence remains unoccupied here
quoted_support: The overall patch generation budget is capped at 50, meaning that the repair process terminates once either all budgets are consumed or a plausible patch is found.
